habitat.naturalHabitat: Skin flora, especially of the perineal/genital area
habitat.hostAssociation: Commensal; opportunistic urinary pathogen mainly in young sexually active women
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Also found in some foods (uncommonly clinically relevant)

culture.colonyMorphology: White to slightly yellow, non-hemolytic colonies

identificationClues: Gram-positive cocci in clusters, coagulase negative
Novobiocin RESISTANT — the key feature distinguishing it from S. epidermidis (sensitive)
Classic cause of uncomplicated UTI in young, sexually active women ("honeymoon cystitis")

clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous, from the patient's own perineal/genital flora
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Second most common cause of uncomplicated community-acquired UTI after E. coli, particularly in young sexually active women
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Novobiocin resistance is the standard bedside/lab differentiator from the novobiocin-sensitive S. epidermidis

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Novobiocin resistance distinguishes it from S. epidermidis
